“Declaration on Government and Law, circa August 1835 [D&C 134],” in Doctrine and Covenants, 1835, 254,josephsmithpapers.org; “Letter to the Elders of the Church, 2 October 1835,” inLatter Day Saints’ Messenger and Advocate,Sept. 1835, 180,josephsmithpapers.org.

Many of these articles were published just after an abolitionist visited Kirtland, and as concerns about Latter-day Saint antislavery and pro-Indian attitudes led to tension with the refugee Saints’ neighbors in Clay County, Missouri. For examples of the Kirtland Saints’ efforts to distance the Church from the abolitionist movement, seeMessenger and Advocate,vol. 2, no. 7 (Apr. 1836), 289–91, 295–96, 299–301 andMessenger and Advocate,vol. 2, no. 8 (May 1836), 313–14. For examples of the pressure on the Missouri Saints and their response, seeMessenger and Advocate,vol. 2, no. 11 (Aug. 1836), 353–55, 359–61.
